newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn warned EU minister failure could hurt euro.
newsitem.headline: Quinn warned EU minister failure could hurt euro.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn warned his colleagues during overnight talks on Friday that failure to agree a budget pact could hurt prospects for the introduction of the new euro currency, EU sources said.

Seeking to persuade finance ministers of the need to find a compromise on a pact to keep budgets sound after the euro's launch, Quinn said there were plenty of people who would be happy to see the EU's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) put off.
"It is not getting any easier. A lot of people out there want to knock this project," he was quoted as telling finance ministers during their 11-hour meeting that ended at 3 a.m. (0300 GMT).

Quinn said that in Ireland's case, for example, delaying EMU would require a referendum because it would mean the Maastricht Treaty, which sets the euro's launch for January 1, 1999 at the latest, would have to be changed.
In an attempt to cajole his colleagues, Quinn also turned to some hallmark plain speaking.
At one point, sources said, he reminded his colleagues of the time by noting that Ireland is renowned for its substantial breakfasts.

He also introduced the compromise document eventually endorsed by the ministers as "the complete ECOFIN bastard", a reference to its mixed heritage. The plan contained parts of ideas floated by Belgium, Ireland and others.
ECOFIN is EU-speak for meetings of economic and finance ministers.
The plan drafted by the ministers calls for countries running excessive deficits to be fined, unless there are exceptional economic circumstances.
It was defining the exceptional circumstances that gave ministers the biggest headache, with Germany holding out for super-strict definitions.

Sources said that Luxembourg Prime Jean-Claude Juncker, who is also the country's finance minister, had told his colleagues that the issue was going to be almost impossible to explain to anyone outside the room.
This presumably included other EU leaders, who were debating the issue on Friday morning.
